sources.credit: NASA Goddard Space Flight Center Image by Reto Stöckli (land surface, shallow water, clouds). Enhancements by Robert Simmon (ocean color, compositing, 3D globes, animation).
sources.note: Download https://assets.science.nasa.gov/content/dam/science/esd/eo/content-feature/bluemarble/images/cloud_combined_2048.jpg, linked from that page (checked 2026-11-04). The page says the cloud image is a composite of two days of visible-light imagery and a third day of thermal infrared over the poles; it does not date those days. The Blue Marble's other MODIS layers are from June to September 2001, so the clouds are most likely from 2001 too [inference]. Cloud cover of a few days, not today's weather.

sources.note: Metres above the EGM2008 geoid (the GeoTIFF's vertical datum, 'WGS 84 + EGM2008 height'), on cells of 1/60 degree from longitude -180 and latitude 90, with no missing values. The surface grid gives the ice surface where there is ice and includes lake and sea floors: Lake Baikal's cells lie hundreds of metres below sea level.

files.note: A Lanczos resample of the input to 8192x4096, JPEG quality 90. The input is kept in data/lookdev/sources, outside git, and pinned by its SHA-256 in the source. Rebaked byte for byte on 2026-11-04 with this repository's locked dependencies.

A Lanczos resample of the input to 8192x4096, with the dim base layer NASA blended in removed by a luminance smoothstep from 0.10 to 0.55, JPEG quality 92. Relative brightness follows NASA's stretched visualization, not calibrated radiance. The input is kept in data/lookdev/sources, outside git, and pinned by its SHA-256 in the source. Rebaked byte for byte on 2026-11-04 with this repository's locked dependencies.

Byte-identical to https://cdn.eso.org/images/large/eso0932a.jpg as downloaded on 2026-11-04; ESO does not distribute the 800-megapixel original. A mosaic of almost 300 fields, each shot four times over 2008 and 2009, stitched by Frederic Tapissier. Plate carree, 360 by 180 degrees, with the galactic plane horizontal; its axes sit 3.78 degrees from galactic, so the renderers sample it through eso0932a_registration.json. The pixels are unchanged; the shader grades the image for display (black level 0.042, power 1.52 and a warm tint). It shows Venus at RA 23h19m, Dec -3.9 and Jupiter at RA 19h30m, Dec -21.9, where they stood when their fields were shot; the repository's ephemeris puts Venus within 0.06 degrees of that point on 2009-01-22 and Jupiter within 0.04 degrees on 2008-06-09 (tests/integration/test_sky_registration.py), dates of agreement rather than capture dates from ESO. Both planets stay in the image, unretouched, and the sky layer's disclosure names them.

The panorama's registration to the catalog stars (docs/science/SKY_PANORAMA_REGISTRATION.md): a rotation from galactic plus a vertical offset, then a smoothed table of the remaining offsets, fitted to 5,021 isolated stars to magnitude 6 from the core tiles of layers 0 and 1, which it pins by one SHA-256, and checked on held-out stars. The panorama's pixels are not changed. `--verify` refits and compares byte for byte on the machine that made the file; tests/integration/test_sky_registration.py allows for platform rounding.
Byte-identical to https://cdn.eso.org/images/screen/eso1804a.jpg as downloaded on 2026-11-04. Formerly eso_lagoon_nebula.jpg, although it shows Lupus 3, not the Lagoon Nebula.
Byte-identical to the kit's lroc_color_poles_1k.jpg as downloaded on 2026-11-04: the 2019 colour map at 1024x512, although the file name says 2k.
Byte-identical to the kit's ldem_3_8bit.jpg as downloaded on 2026-11-04: an 8-bit LOLA elevation map at 1024x512, for which the page gives no height scale.

Water cover, 4096x2048, equirectangular from longitude -180 and latitude 90: 255 is water (ocean, lakes and reservoirs), 0 is land, and a coast pixel holds the fraction of its area under water, measured on four lines per pixel row. Land below sea level stays land.

Heights, 4096x2048, equirectangular from longitude -180 and latitude 90: the mean over each pixel's ETOPO cells, in metres above EGM2008. Each pixel stores round(height + 11000) in R and G; decode as R * 256 + G - 11000. B is always 0 and there is no alpha, so load it as data, without colour conversion. Lake and sea floors are included: where earth_water_natural_earth_4k.png marks water, the height is the floor, not the water surface.

A Lanczos resample of the base map to 8192x4096, JPEG quality 90, as for earth_day_bluemarble_2004-11_8k.jpg, whose source has relief shading baked in. With earth_height_etopo2022_4k.png, relief is lit once, by the renderer.
